section: States Reorganisation Commission (Fazl Ali) and the States Reorganisation Act 1956
subsections: SRC - date set up, chairman, members, report
States Reorganisation Act 1956 - states, UTs, amendment

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Submission of the States Reorganisation Commission report
B. Announcement of the States Reorganisation Commission in the Lok Sabha
C. Formal constitution of the Commission by Home Ministry Resolution
D. Coming into force of the States Reorganisation Act
accepted.x: The Commission was announced on 22 December 1953, formally constituted on 29 December 1953, submitted its report in 1955, and the States Reorganisation Act came into force on 1 November 1956.
accepted.tq: Use the first-and-last method, then place the two closely related 1953 events carefully.
accepted.sec: SRC - date set up, chairman, members, report

accepted.s: The States Reorganisation Commission was formally constituted through which of the following instruments?
accepted.x: The Commission was formally constituted on 29 December 1953 through Home Ministry Resolution No. 53/69/53 (CDX).
accepted.tq: Identify the exact issuing authority instead of relying only on the resolution number.
accepted.sec: SRC - date set up, chairman, members, report

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the report of the States Reorganisation Commission:
1. It was submitted in 1955.
2. It recommended the abolition of the Part A, Part B and Part C classification.
3. It recommended the creation of 16 states and 3 Union Territories.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The report was submitted in 1955 and proposed 16 states and 3 Union Territories along with abolition of the Part A, B and C classification.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical and institutional recommendation separately before choosing the coded combination.
accepted.sec: SRC - date set up, chairman, members, report

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Commission or Committee)
a. S.K. Dhar Commission
b. JVP Committee
c. States Reorganisation Commission

i. Rejected language as the sole basis and considered wider factors
 ii. Preferred administrative convenience over language
 iii. Rejected language as the basis for reorganising states

The correct matching is:
accepted.x: The S.K. Dhar Commission preferred administrative convenience, the JVP Committee rejected language as the basis, and the States Reorganisation Commission treated language as important but not the sole factor.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure association between the Dhar Commission and administrative convenience.
accepted.sec: SRC - date set up, chairman, members, report

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly indicates the positions held by the members of the States Reorganisation Commission at the time of its constitution?
o: Syed Fazl Ali—Governor of Odisha; H.N. Kunzru—Member, Council of States; K.M. Panikkar—diplomat
Syed Fazl Ali—Governor of Punjab; H.N. Kunzru—Member, Lok Sabha; K.M. Panikkar—Chief Minister
Syed Fazl Ali—Chief Justice of India; H.N. Kunzru—Governor of Odisha; K.M. Panikkar—Member, Council of States
Syed Fazl Ali—diplomat; H.N. Kunzru—Governor of Odisha; K.M. Panikkar—Member, Council of States
accepted.x: Syed Fazl Ali was the Governor of Odisha, H.N. Kunzru was a Member of the Council of States, and K.M. Panikkar was a diplomat.
accepted.tq: Match each person with the office held at that time, watching for swapped-authority traps.
accepted.sec: SRC - date set up, chairman, members, report

accepted.s: The States Reorganisation Commission received approximately how many memorandums?
accepted.x: The Commission received 1,52,250 memorandums during its consideration of the reorganisation question.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact figure from nearby rearrangements of the same digits.
accepted.sec: SRC - date set up, chairman, members, report

accepted.s: The appointment of the States Reorganisation Commission was primarily necessitated by which development?
o: The creation of Andhra State leading to similar demands in other regions
The acceptance of the Punjabi Suba demand
The merger of Hyderabad with Mysore
The demand for a separate Pakistan after Partition
accepted.x: The creation of Andhra State in 1953 intensified similar demands elsewhere, prompting the appointment of the Commission.
accepted.tq: Link the institutional response to its immediate historical trigger.
accepted.sec: SRC - date set up, chairman, members, report

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT treated by the States Reorganisation Commission as a factor in reorganising states?
o: Exclusive dependence on a single language
accepted.x: The Commission rejected the principle of 'one language, one state'. It considered language along with administrative efficiency, economic viability, contiguity and national unity.
accepted.tq: Find the extreme word that converts a genuine factor into an exclusive principle.
accepted.sec: SRC - date set up, chairman, members, report

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the States Reorganisation Commission:
1. It regarded language as an important factor but not the only factor.
2. It accepted the principle that every language must have one separate state.
3. It also considered national unity while making recommendations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because the Commission rejected the formula of 'one language, one state'.
accepted.tq: Test the difference between treating language as an important factor and making it the exclusive rule.
accepted.sec: SRC - date set up, chairman, members, report

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the first linguistic state created in India after Independence?
accepted.x: Andhra State, formed in 1953, was the first linguistic state created after Independence. Orissa had been the first province formed on linguistic lines in 1936.
accepted.tq: Separate the pre-Independence distinction from the post-Independence one.
accepted.sec: SRC - date set up, chairman, members, report

accepted.s:
With reference to the arguments supporting linguistic states, consider the following statements:
1. They enabled people to be governed in their own language.
2. They helped preserve cultural identity.
3. They could make administration easier.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three were recognised arguments in favour of linguistic states: governance in the people's language, preservation of cultural identity and easier administration.
accepted.tq: Recognise a cluster of related positive effects rather than selecting only the most familiar one.
accepted.sec: SRC - date set up, chairman, members, report

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT an argument advanced against the creation of linguistic states?
o: Fear of threats to national unity after Partition
accepted.x: The arguments against linguistic states included fears regarding unity, regionalism, border disputes and minority disputes. Elimination of administrative difficulties was not an argument against them.
accepted.tq: Identify the option that does not belong to the stated group of apprehensions.
accepted.sec: SRC - date set up, chairman, members, report

accepted.s: The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 came into force on:
accepted.x: The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 came into force on 1 November 1956.
accepted.tq: Use the exact commencement date rather than the year of enactment alone.
accepted.sec: States Reorganisation Act 1956 - states, UTs, amendment

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents states included in the reorganisation brought about in 1956?
o: Andhra Pradesh, bilingual Bombay, Punjab, enlarged Madras, Mysore and Kerala
Andhra Pradesh, bilingual Bombay, Rajasthan, Orissa, Mysore and Kerala
Andhra Pradesh, Hyderabad, Gujarat, Punjab, Madras and Travancore-Cochin
Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Haryana, Mysore and Kerala
accepted.x: The reorganised units included merged Andhra Pradesh, bilingual Bombay and Punjab, enlarged Madras, Mysore and Kerala. Gujarat, Maharashtra and Haryana were formed later.
accepted.tq: Reject options that insert later states or pre-existing units in place of the 1956 arrangement.
accepted.sec: States Reorganisation Act 1956 - states, UTs, amendment

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT among the Union Territories created under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956?
accepted.x: The Union Territories included Delhi, Manipur, Tripura, Himachal Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and Laccadive-Minicoy-Amindivi. Goa was not among them.
accepted.tq: Check the named list and identify the geographically related but absent territory.
accepted.sec: States Reorganisation Act 1956 - states, UTs, amendment

accepted.s: The distinction among Part A, Part B, Part C and Part D units was abolished by which constitutional amendment?
accepted.x: The Seventh Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956 abolished the Part A, B, C and D classification and created the categories of States and Union Territories.
accepted.tq: Pair the constitutional change with the amendment number and year, avoiding nearby amendment-number traps.
accepted.sec: States Reorganisation Act 1956 - states, UTs, amendment

accepted.s: Kerala was formed in 1956 mainly by combining:
accepted.x: Kerala was formed by combining Travancore-Cochin with the Malabar region.
accepted.tq: Test the exact territorial components of a newly formed state.
accepted.sec: States Reorganisation Act 1956 - states, UTs, amendment

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 is correct?
o: The Telugu districts of Hyderabad were retained as a Union Territory.
The Telangana region of Hyderabad State joined Andhra to form Andhra Pradesh.
Andhra Pradesh was formed by merging Madras and Mysore.
The coastal districts of Andhra joined Bombay to form Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.x: The Telangana region of Hyderabad State joined Andhra State to form Andhra Pradesh under the 1956 reorganisation.
accepted.tq: Track the actual territorial merger and reject reversals involving neighbouring states.
accepted.sec: States Reorganisation Act 1956 - states, UTs, amendment

accepted.s: Which state was the first to be formed under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh was the first state formed under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first state formed after Independence from the first state formed specifically under the 1956 Act.
accepted.sec: States Reorganisation Act 1956 - states, UTs, amendment

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 amended which provision of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 to substitute the expression referring to Andhra Pradesh and Telangana?
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 later amended Section 15 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 to read 'Andhra Pradesh and Telangana'.
accepted.tq: Match the later amendment with the precise section number rather than the Act number alone.
accepted.sec: States Reorganisation Act 1956 - states, UTs, amendment

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the recommendations for Hyderabad State:

List-I (Region)
a. Raichur and Gulbarga
b. Marathwada
c. Telugu districts

i. Bombay
 ii. Mysore
 iii. Separate Hyderabad State

The correct matching is:
accepted.x: Raichur and Gulbarga were assigned to Mysore, Marathwada to Bombay, and the Telugu districts were to remain as a separate Hyderabad State.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair of the Kannada districts with Mysore and eliminate the remaining codes.
accepted.sec: SRC recommendations - Hyderabad/Telangana, Vidarbha, Bombay

accepted.s: After the proposed division of Hyderabad State, the residual Hyderabad State was envisaged as comprising:
o: The Kannada-speaking districts with Gulbarga as capital
The Telugu-speaking districts of the former Nizam's state with Hyderabad city as capital
The Marathi-speaking districts with Aurangabad as capital
The entire former Hyderabad State with Secunderabad as a Union Territory
accepted.x: The residual Hyderabad State was to consist of the Telugu-speaking districts of the former Nizam's state, with Hyderabad city as its capital.
accepted.tq: Separate the residual territory from the districts transferred to Mysore and Bombay.
accepted.sec: SRC recommendations - Hyderabad/Telangana, Vidarbha, Bombay

accepted.s: What was the specific recommendation of the States Reorganisation Commission regarding Vidarbha?
o: It should be merged with Hyderabad State.
It should be made a Union Territory.
It should form a separate state.
It should be divided between Bombay and Madhya Pradesh.
accepted.x: The Commission recommended the creation of a separate Vidarbha state.
accepted.tq: Identify the Commission's recommendation directly instead of substituting the later territorial outcome.
accepted.sec: SRC recommendations - Hyderabad/Telangana, Vidarbha, Bombay

accepted.s: The States Reorganisation Commission recommended that Bombay should be:
o: Divided immediately into Gujarat and Maharashtra
Retained as a bilingual state comprising Gujarati and Marathi areas
accepted.x: The Commission recommended retaining Bombay as a bilingual state consisting of Gujarati- and Marathi-speaking areas.
accepted.tq: Watch for later developments being projected backward onto the 1955 recommendation.
accepted.sec: SRC recommendations - Hyderabad/Telangana, Vidarbha, Bombay

accepted.s: Which of the following demands was NOT accepted by the States Reorganisation Commission?
o: Separate Hyderabad State for the Telugu districts
accepted.x: The Punjabi Suba demand was not accepted. The Commission did recommend a separate Vidarbha, bilingual Bombay and a separate Hyderabad State for the Telugu districts.
accepted.tq: Use the recommendation list to identify the rejected demand rather than a transferred territory.
accepted.sec: SRC recommendations - Hyderabad/Telangana, Vidarbha, Bombay

accepted.s: According to the relevant demographic consideration in the recommendations concerning Hyderabad-Secunderabad, what percentage of the people spoke Urdu?
accepted.x: The stated figure was 45.4 percent of the people in Hyderabad-Secunderabad speaking Urdu.
accepted.tq: Handle percentage options by comparing the decimal and digit order carefully.
accepted.sec: SRC recommendations - Hyderabad/Telangana, Vidarbha, Bombay

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the SRC recommendations on Urdu in Hyderabad-Secunderabad:
1. The Commission recommended special status for Urdu in education and administration.
2. It recommended non-discrimination in recruitment.
3. It recommended that the twin cities be made a Union Territory.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Commission rejected making Hyderabad-Secunderabad a Union Territory.
accepted.tq: Separate the accepted safeguards for Urdu from the rejected territorial proposal.
accepted.sec: SRC recommendations - Hyderabad/Telangana, Vidarbha, Bombay

accepted.s: Why did the States Reorganisation Commission reject the plea to keep Hyderabad undivided?
o: It accepted the Punjabi Suba demand instead.
It considered the Telugu districts economically unviable.
It intended to transfer all Hyderabad districts to Mysore.
It sought to preserve the 200-year-old Deccani culture.
accepted.x: The plea to keep Hyderabad undivided was made to preserve the 200-year-old Deccani culture, but the Commission did not accept that plea.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the stated reason behind a plea from the Commission's final territorial recommendation.
accepted.sec: SRC recommendations - Hyderabad/Telangana, Vidarbha, Bombay
